title: Quiz 6 — Mole Ratios
subject: Chemistry
sourceText:
AP Chemistry — Quiz 6: Mole Ratios
Name: ________

Ammonia is produced by the balanced equation
    N₂ + 3 H₂ → 2 NH₃

Worked example: from 2.0 mol N₂ the conversion is
    2.0 mol N₂ × (2 mol NH₃ / 1 mol N₂) = 4.0 mol NH₃
using the coefficients as a mole ratio.

A sealed flask is charged with 4.0 mol N₂ and 9.0 mol H₂.
The theoretical yield is the amount of NH₃ made by the limiting reagent.

1) How many moles of NH₃ can form from 4.0 mol N₂ if H₂ is unlimited?
2) How many moles of NH₃ can form from 9.0 mol H₂ if N₂ is unlimited?
3) Name the limiting reagent and state the theoretical yield of NH₃.

Note: leftover moles of the excess reactant stay unused — they never re-enter the product step.

marks.label: the mole ratio
marks.why: The quiz multiplies by (2 mol NH₃ / 1 mol N₂) without naming the move — that's how every later item converts one formula into another.

steps.text: A balanced equation is a recipe in moles: 1 mol N₂ reacts with 3 mol H₂ to make 2 mol NH₃.
To change substances, build a fraction from those coefficients — target on top, given on the bottom.
Multiply the given moles by that fraction. The given unit cancels; moles of the target remain.
In the worked example, 2.0 mol N₂ × (2 mol NH₃ / 1 mol N₂) = 4.0 mol NH₃. The 2/1 is the mole ratio.

check.prompt: Apply the move: N₂ + 3 H₂ → 2 NH₃. How many moles of NH₃ form from 4.0 mol N₂?

marks.label: the limiting reagent
marks.why: Item 3 cites the limiting reagent as the source of the theoretical yield but never shows the two-yield comparison that names it.

steps.text: When two amounts are given, each reactant can make its own amount of the same product.
Convert each given amount through the mole ratio into moles of that product.
The smaller product amount is the theoretical yield. The reactant that made it is limiting.
On this quiz: 4.0 mol N₂ → 8.0 mol NH₃; 9.0 mol H₂ → 6.0 mol NH₃. H₂ is limiting, so the yield is 6.0 mol.

check.prompt: Apply the move: 4.0 mol N₂ and 9.0 mol H₂ react by N₂ + 3 H₂ → 2 NH₃. Which reactant is limiting?

nextLine.setup: A later problem says: '9.0 mol H₂ × (2 mol NH₃ / 3 mol H₂). Write the next line — evaluate that product yourself.'

expect.hint: Multiply across, then divide: 9.0 × 2 is 18, and 18/3 is 6. The next line is 6.0 mol NH₃.
